# Voice designer

- Route: `/tools/voice-designer`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `ai`
- Slug: `voice-designer`

## Summary

Describe a voice in words, preview it, and keep the one you like to read any text in more than twenty languages. (AI tools)

## Details

The voice designer creates a voice that does not belong to anyone. Describe it in a few words, such as gender, age, accent, tone and pace, or build the description from the chips, and preview a sample sentence. Previews are free, three per description each hour. When you hear the one you want, give it a name and keep it: the exact voice you previewed is saved to your account and can then read any text, in any language of the speech tool. Designing runs on Qwen3-TTS and speaking on Chatterbox, both on our own GPU server, and every generated file carries an inaudible watermark.
### What it does
- Turns a text description of a voice into a spoken preview.
- Keeps the exact previewed voice (the same seed) when you save it.
- Speaks any text with the kept voice in over 20 languages.
- Returns an MP3 of the speech, with a WAV download made in your browser.
### How to use it
1. Describe: Write or click the traits you want.
2. Preview: Three free previews per description each hour.
3. Keep it: Name the voice and save it to your account.
4. Generate speech: Type any text and download the audio.
### Supported formats
- Input: text
- Output: mp3, wav
- Previews: 3 per description per hour, not counted.
- Keeping a voice needs an account.
### Technical details
- Designing uses Qwen3-TTS VoiceDesign (Apache 2.0). The preview sentence can be rendered in ten languages: Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, German, French, Russian, Portuguese, Spanish and Italian.
- A kept voice is stored as its description, the seed and a 10-second reference clip; from then on Chatterbox speaks it, so it sounds the same everywhere and in every supported language.
- Previews are not counted. Keeping a voice counts as one AI job, and each generation counts as one AI job.
- Descriptions work best in English; the chips add English traits.
### Use cases
- Characters: Give each character in a story or a game prototype its own voice.
- Explainers: A calm, clear narrator for product and training videos.
- Placeholder audio: Temporary voice-over while a script is still changing.
- Accessibility: A pleasant reading voice for long documents.
### FAQ
Q: Is a designed voice someone's real voice?
A: No. It is generated from your description and a random seed; it is not modelled on any particular person.
Q: Why do previews run out?
A: Each description can be previewed three times an hour so the free previews stay available for everyone. Change the description to preview again, or keep the voice you like.
Q: Will the kept voice sound like the preview?
A: Yes. Keeping sends the same description and seed as the preview you heard, and the voice is saved from that render.
Q: Which languages can it speak?
A: A voice is designed in one of ten languages, and once kept it can speak every language of the speech tool, more than twenty in all.
Q: Is the output marked as generated?
A: Yes. Every generated file carries an inaudible watermark that detection tools can read.
